output.answer:
**Berkshire Hathaway cash pile — latest picture (Q2 2026)**

| Period | Cash + T-bills |
|---|---|
| End 2022 | ~$129B |
| End 2025 | ~$373B |
| Q1 2026 | **$397.4B (record)** |
| Q2 2026 | **~$365B** (–4%, first sequential drop in 3+ years) |

**Key points**
- The peak of ~$397 billion came in Q1 2026 — Berkshire's all-time high, and reportedly more than Apple, Amazon, Alphabet, and Microsoft combined. It was large enough to buy almost any S&P 500 company outright.
- The decline in Q2 2026 was Greg Abel's first quarter as CEO (Buffett stepped back in January 2026). Berkshire became a **net buyer of equities for the first time in 14 quarters**, buying ~$23.5B of stocks vs. ~$3.7B sold.
- Notable deployment: a **$6.8B purchase of homebuilder Taylor Morrison** and a **$10B investment in Alphabet**, plus **$4.5B in buybacks**.
- Context: Buffett built the reserve by selling roughly **$173B net of equities over 2022–2024**, parking proceeds in short-term Treasuries while waiting for cheaper valuations. Berkshire also sharply cut its Apple stake (from a peak of ~915M shares to ~228M).

**Read on it:** The shrinking pile signals a strategic pivot — Abel appears more willing to deploy capital than Buffett was in recent years, though the reserve remains historically enormous. As a percentage of total assets, the cash was the highest since at least 1998 at its peak.
